statement: Breach of contract — the full invoiced amount is owed. Goods were delivered and accepted, the invoice is unpaid, and no written rejection exists within the contractual window (§7).
evidenceFor: Signed contract with delivery and payment obligations
Written acceptance of the delivered goods ('the cake was perfect')
Invoice unpaid past its due date
No written rejection within the §7 window
evidenceAgainst: Claim targets an individual employee rather than the business (ethics guard)
discriminatingTests: Is there any written rejection of the goods within 5 days of delivery?
Is the claim against the client business entity (not an employee)?

statement: Partial liability — a valid quality setoff reduces the amount owed. The buyer complained about quality and rejected the goods in writing within the §7 window.
evidenceFor: A written rejection within the §7 window exists
evidenceAgainst: The only complaint was a phone call — nothing in writing
The buyer accepted the goods in writing after delivery
discriminatingTests: Did the buyer send any written rejection within 5 days of delivery?

statement: No breach — the rejection was justified and nothing is owed. The goods were not accepted and the buyer rejected them in writing.
evidenceAgainst: The client's own email accepts the delivery ('the cake was perfect')
The receipt is signed by the client's office manager
discriminatingTests: Did the client accept the delivery in writing?
